reason: Exact: 'flower head' is the common English name of the capitulum. This follows the earlier rule C262 (head -> capitulum inflorescence). Counts such as 'flower heads 25-30' are numbers of capitula per plant.

target: trichome (PO_0000282; 'scale' is a synonym) part_of rhizome (PO_0004542), margin region
reason: These are the margins of the scales on fern rhizomes. PO treats scales as trichomes. The patterns can express this as the margin region of a scale qualified by its rhizome. The qualities (entire, dentate, denticulate, pale) all describe edges.

A leaf-anatomy layer named in contrast to a true hypodermis, so mapping it to hypodermis (PO_0005051) would be wrong. The examples give only present/absent, with no organ or definition to place a new class safely. Leave it to a curator.

target: leaf stomatal complex (PO_0025183), counted as rows per leaf surface (abaxial/adaxial position)
reason: In conifer floras these are rows or bands of stomata on each side of the leaf. The bearer is the leaf stomatal complex in a series; the number of rows per surface is a count over that series, not a new structure.
A position word ('abaxial spines', 'abaxial and adaxial'). The noun it qualifies is missing; this is a fragment.
A shape or arrangement word ('ring of hairs', 'anneau de poils'), not a structure. The bare 'ring' was already rejected as a generic part.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of leaf lamina margin (PO_0025009)
reason: Bryophyte leaf description: the cells along the leaf margin, as opposed to median cells. This is expressible as a cell qualified by the margin region of the lamina.
Exact: the plural of an existing FLOPO class. PO also lists bulbil as a synonym of aerial tuber (PO_0004548), but the FLOPO class is the reviewed target.
An adverb modifying 'stalked' or 'petiolulate'. A fragment.
Narrower: the plural of 'veinlet', which rule C270 already maps to leaf lamina vein. PO lists veinlet as a synonym of the higher-order veins under that class.

'Filament' here is not the stamen filament: these are cell rows ('filaments of 4-8 cells', with papillae per cell), as on moss leaves or on staminal hairs. Which filament is meant cannot be told without context.

Narrower: in FNA usage the root crown is the short perennial stem base at the top of the taproot, multibranched and woolly. This matches the earlier caudex->stem decision (C252). It is not the hypocotyl-root junction or 'crown root'.

label: stelidium
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of gynostemium (FLOPO_0986015)
definition: One of a pair of tooth-, arm- or wing-like appendages at the apex or the sides of the gynostemium (column) of some orchids, especially Pleurothallidinae and Oncidiinae.
reason: A distinct orchid structure that floras count, shape and measure. No PO or FLOPO class exists, and the generic 'appendage' was rejected. Propose it to PO together with gynostemium.
Exact: the curator decision of 2026-09-18 maps 'lower surface of the leaf' to PO_0000049, since PO models surfaces as epidermis.

In bipinnate fern and legume leaves this is the axis of a pinna (hairy, winged, up to 1 cm). It can be expressed as the leaf rachis qualified by the pinna. Where it means an inflorescence axis, it would not apply.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to ('bracteate units', 'phloem units').

Consistent with the earlier rejection of 'areole' as generic. Where the head is a leaf or lamina, leaf lamina areole (PO_0025392) applies, but here some uses are on other organs ('400-500 areolae on each side').
Exact in practice: not a real botanical term. Every example reads 'involucre(s) cylindric/hemispheric, tomentose', so this is a mis-normalized 'involucre'. Fix the normalization as well.
Exact: PO has the class, with 'leaf lamina teeth' as a synonym.
Narrower: a beard is a zone or tuft of hairs, for example on Iris falls. Its colour and stiffness are qualities of those hairs. The having-a-beard quality is already 'bearded' (FLOPO:0991118).
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. The singular 'cell' was rejected in the previous review.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. Compare the earlier rejection of 'lateral lobe'.
Exact once the quality is stripped: 'midrib' is a synonym of leaf midvein and 'present' is the quality. Where the bearer is a lobe of another organ, use the lobe's own midvein.

PO tubercle (PO_0025352) is the cactus podarium, but floras use 'tubercles' for wart-like outgrowths on seeds, fruits, stems and leaves. Without the organ the meaning is unclear; on a known organ, 'tuberculate' as a quality is better.
Crisped or erose lip-lobe margins are orchid labellum descriptions, so this is the margin region of an existing class. In Lamiaceae or Acanthaceae contexts use corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) instead.

target: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part_of corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017), lower position
reason: The lobes of the lower corolla lip of two-lipped corollas, counted ('lower lip lobes 2', '3-lobed'). Expressible as a lobe in the lower position of the lip.
Narrower: in Myrtaceae, Melastomataceae and similar families, the lobes on the hypanthium rim are the calyx lobes (oblong, acute, 4 per flower). The hypanthium itself has no lobes of its own.
A shape quality of hairs or scales ('stellate hairs', 'stellate scales'); the noun is missing.
A measurement used as the second term of a relative length ('leaves 1/2-2/3 of stem length'). The bearer is the leaf and the reference is the stem (PO_0009047).
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. This follows the earlier rejection of 'callus'. Callosities occur on orchid lips, legume standards, fruits and leaf margins.
